review_issue_summaries.summary: Save/export workflow for the four non-character card types is copied into four editors with no owning lib module
protocol.ts re-declares CardType identically to LibraryCardType and the two are joined by unchecked casts
mcp/tsconfig.json declares only half the app modules the MCP package actually imports, and nothing enforces their browser-neutrality
Lorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona editors each re-implement the same card-editor lifecycle; no module owns it
The five-member card-type vocabulary is redeclared in five modules and cast between, so no module owns it
The blank character card exists twice — in lib/tavernCard.ts and in the Ronan Voss template file the app actually uses
personaParser/personaLlm are named for a persona-only past but now own text parsing for every card type
minimalPng.ts claims a minimalPng.test.ts verifies its bytes; that test does not exist
DecodePNG classifies cards by metadata keyword alone and re-declares CHARACTER_KEYS, while ImportPNG uses lib/cardShape
Bridge openCard preserves the library id for characters but routes the other four card types through id-less import handlers
useUnsavedWarning guards character editing only; the four sibling editors hold the same unsaved React state without it
ScriptEditor's CodeEditor is styled with inline hex colours while all other components use the semantic Tailwind tokens
The same five card kinds are declared as four separately named unions, forcing casts between structurally identical types
src/lib mixes single-file directories with flat files of the same size, with no visible rule separating the two
Library.tsx runs four IndexedDB/zip I/O paths with no error handling and sticky busy flags
Save-to-library catches drop the error message the sibling export path reports verbatim
readImageFile's designed rejection has no handler at either call site
Every localStorage read is guarded with a default; every write is bare
Two competing idioms for narrowing unknown in catch: `as Error` cast vs instanceof check
runEndpoint's blanket fetch catch reports every failure as 'server not running', including aborts
MCP create_script names the script body `code` while every consumer reads ScriptCard.content, so the body is silently dropped
saveAnyCard cannot save any card - its signature explicitly excludes the character type
Library's `refreshToken` prop is a third meaning of "token" in a codebase where token already means a pairing secret and an LLM token
SmartImportPanel aliases the narrow SorterSettings type to the broad name `Settings` on the line above importing a component actually called SorterSettings
Two different functions both named processFile - a generic verb in domain code where the domain has precise words
The MCP content-envelope helper is named `text`, which collides with a real `text` tool parameter and forces an alias
bridge/client.ts has a module-private `open()` sitting alongside an `openCard()` that means something entirely different
LibraryCard fakes a tagged union, forcing 17 unchecked casts to recover the type it already knows
The same five-member card-type union is declared four times, costing five casts to convert between identical types
Four non-character editors re-implement an identical state/save/export host with no shared abstraction
ImportPNG and DecodePNG each take five parallel onLoad* callbacks that App satisfies with eight near-identical handlers
gpt-tokenizer's 2.2 MB o200k BPE table is statically imported, making up most of the 2.49 MB entry chunk
mcp/tsconfig.json lists only 2 of the 4 app-source files the MCP server imports across the package boundary
start.sh/start.bat install dependencies only when node_modules is absent, so dependency changes never reach an existing install
Four card editors repeat the same state block and save/export helpers near-verbatim
App.tsx keeps four parallel key/init state pairs and eight handlers that differ only by card type
uint8ToDataUrl is written twice, at module scope in one file and inside a callback in its sibling
decodeCharaFromPng inlines iTXt pointer arithmetic and nested try/catch three levels deep
encodeCharaToPng's chunk partition has an unreachable IHDR guard and a needlessly mutable binding
deleteEntry mixes a functional updater with a stale outer read and picks an arbitrary survivor
getCardTokenBreakdown declares nine locals and hand-sums them; the 3000 ceiling is restated in the UI
DecodePNG routes payloads by metadata key with its own CHARACTER_KEYS copy, ignoring lib/cardShape
Lorebook normalisation lives inside LoreBookEditor, so PNG and bridge imports pass raw payloads through an `as LoreBook` cast
Five parallel per-card-type callbacks repeated across App, Library, ImportPNG and DecodePNG, plus a dead pngData param
Bridge persist() saves characters with pngData null and platform hardcoded, so an MCP update wipes both
MCP create_script sends `code` but ScriptCard/ScriptEditor read `content`, so agent-created scripts arrive empty
Bridge invents findCard() over getAllCards() because the library module exposes no get-by-id
No test environment configured, so all 30 components and 5 hooks are untestable, not just untested
Security-critical HMAC handshake in bridge/protocol.ts is pure and node-testable but has zero tests
The MCP server package shares the wire protocol with the app but has no tests and no test script
